remarks: No tracked port carries a weather or closure entry this run, and that is the correct state rather than a gap. Nothing in the tracked set is suspended, and the one live cyclone stays about a thousand kilometres clear of the nearest of them.

Dujuan is the only active system and it is not a supply-chain event for these ports. It has strengthened from tropical storm to severe tropical storm since the previous read on 16 September, but the forecast track runs northwest then northeast into open water east of Japan. Its closest approach to any tracked port is 997 km, at Busan, roughly three days out. That is well outside the 600 km threat radius, so no threat rows are written.

The congestion at Shanghai/Ningbo is now a queue problem, not a weather problem. Saudel and Krovanh have been gone for a fortnight and the backlog they left has merged with the pre-Golden Week export rush. SEKO still reports 7-8 day berth waits at Waigaoqiao and 7 days at Yangshan, with Ningbo Meishan down to 5 days. Deliberately no port entry is written for them: a weather entry would suppress the site's own congestion flag for exactly the ports where that flag should be firing.

Two real stoppages happened in the last week but neither is at a tracked port: gale-force winds shut Dalian for 32 hours and Lianyungang for 14.5 hours. At tracked ports the only interruptions were short navigation-channel closures from the seasonal fishing fleet, 8.8 hours at Shanghai Yangshan and 4 hours at Ningbo. Those are recurring seasonal traffic events, not extraordinary weather, and they are over.

One scheduled stoppage worth planning around, though it is a holiday rather than weather: Busan terminals halt completely for 24 hours from 25 to 26 September for Chuseok. China's Golden Week follows on 1-7 October.

Note on the congestion data this run: Linerlytica has published no new snapshot since 13 September, so the congestion figures behind the site are five days old. No values were invented to fill the gap.
